nodes.label: Levels of Black-Box Explanation
nodes.rationale: Black boxes can be explained via post-hoc surrogate models approximating their function, local/global importance of input factors, or representation learning of interpretable latent factors.

nodes.label: Explainable Models
nodes.rationale: Explainable models give knowledge of which input factors affect the output and how much they affect the decision, even when the model itself is not transparent.

nodes.label: Interpretability vs Accuracy Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Going from linear regression, decision trees, KNN, random forests and SVMs to deep learning raises accuracy but lowers interpretability, which is why black-box models need explanation methods.

nodes.label: Interpretable vs Explainable Model Spectrum
nodes.rationale: Models are placed on a spectrum: decision trees and linear/logistic regression are interpretable, random forests are a grey area, and neural networks/CNNs need post-hoc explanation.

nodes.label: Interpretable / Transparent Models
nodes.rationale: Model is readily understandable, gives a direct explanation, lets one know what each node represents and determine cause and effect.

nodes.label: Model Agnostic Explanation Approaches
nodes.rationale: Preferred for model flexibility, explanation flexibility and representation flexibility: the same explainer works across any fitted model.

nodes.label: Permutation Feature Importance (PFI)
nodes.rationale: Importance = drop in model score (e.g. accuracy) when one feature column is randomly shuffled K times, breaking its link to the target. Simple, global, model-agnostic, works for black-box estimators. Drawbacks: no in-depth view of decisions, ignores feature interactions, explains the whole dataset not individual samples, and adds randomness via reshuffling.

nodes.label: Representation Learning Explanation (Latent Factors)
nodes.rationale: Explain a model by knowing what each node represents, the latent factors behind the decision, and how important each node is to performance.

nodes.label: KernelSHAP
nodes.rationale: Combines linear LIME with Shapley values via a specific proximity kernel to estimate SHAP values model-agnostically; still computationally expensive.

nodes.label: Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME)
nodes.rationale: Locally faithful explanations from a locally linear surrogate model weighted by a proximity measure; accurate while keeping model flexibility, understandable by non-experts, and cheap to switch models. Gives qualitative understanding of input-response relations.

nodes.label: Multicollinearity in Feature Importance
nodes.rationale: A feature's importance can be underestimated under multicollinearity; evaluating all feature subsets and weighting the differences (Shapley sampling values) addresses this.

nodes.label: Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)
nodes.rationale: Treats each explanation as a surrogate model and uses game theory to guarantee a unique additive attribution satisfying local accuracy, missingness and consistency; improves over LIME and handles multicollinearity well. Drawbacks: exponential subset evaluation, high cost even with KernelSHAP, local approximators may still not reveal model behaviour, and time-series dependencies are ignored.

nodes.norm_label: data leakage / data bleeding between train and test beats
nodes.rationale: Beats from the same patient share morphology (electrode placement, conditions, medication), so random beat shuffling puts near-duplicates in train and test, inflating results.

nodes.label: Class V (Premature ventricular contraction)
nodes.description: Broad monophasic QRS (~5) without sharp Q/S dips.

nodes.label: Class f (Fusion of paced and normal beat)
nodes.description: Clean baseline, sharp positive peak (~5) followed by deep negative spike (~-4), biphasic.
nodes.norm_label: class f (fusion of paced and normal beat)

nodes.label: Class R (Right bundle branch block beat)
nodes.description: Double-peaked (rSR') QRS followed by a deep wide trough to ~-3.
nodes.norm_label: class r (right bundle branch block beat)

nodes.label: Class A (Atrial premature beat)
nodes.description: Narrow QRS very similar to N; differs mainly in timing/P-wave, hard to separate from N by morphology alone.

nodes.label: Class N (Normal beat)
nodes.description: Narrow tall QRS (~7), small P wave, flat baseline.

nodes.label: Class / (Paced beat)
nodes.description: Small pacing spike then wide deep negative complex (~-2.6) and broad positive T-wave; very smooth, low-noise trace.

nodes.label: Class F (Fusion of ventricular and normal beat)
nodes.description: Small pre-wave then tall QRS (~5) with S dip; intermediate between N and V.
nodes.norm_label: class f (fusion of ventricular and normal beat)

nodes.label: Class L (Left bundle branch block beat)
nodes.description: Wide, notched QRS followed by deep negative deflection and slow recovery.
nodes.norm_label: class l (left bundle branch block beat)

nodes.label: Per-beat amplitude standardisation (z-score)
nodes.rationale: Baselines sit near 0 and peaks reach several units, consistent with z-score normalisation removing inter-patient amplitude differences.

nodes.label: Fixed-length R-peak-centred beat window (~275 samples)
nodes.rationale: Every beat is aligned with its QRS peak near sample ~138, so each sample index is a comparable feature for SVM/Random Forest.

nodes.label: Spike at sample 0 (edge artifact)
nodes.rationale: N, L, R, V, A and F beats show an abrupt jump at index 0 that drops to baseline immediately; likely a filtering/segmentation boundary artifact rather than physiology. Could act as a spurious feature.
